statements.statement: Two local earmarks in the FY26 state budget ($30,000 for school guidance/mental health/special ed support and $40,000 for a school security system upgrade) had been reported pulled back but have in fact flowed to the state agencies; the town requested the funds quickly.

An outside CPA firm is taking over the entire FY25 closeout; free cash will likely not be certified by special town meeting, but since no appropriations from free cash are planned at that meeting there should be no impact.
New growth actuals for FY26 are coming in substantially higher than the budgeted estimate; the committee disputed the exact figure and asked staff to confirm it with the assessor.
A member reported new growth is now understood to be about $1.3 million, driven by corrected assessed value findings ($979) and higher personal property ($398 instead of $60), pending confirmation.
The library is expected to need additional unanticipated funds to cover a series of maternity leaves, but the amount has not yet been estimated.
Transitioning employees to a new vacation system under the proposed SAP/personnel bylaw changes will have a cost that could not yet be quantified pending the attorney's final language.
PAC (public access) is sustaining its operations on retained earnings because its fee revenue is running below its operating needs.
